payload.text: (2026-09-18 08:27Z, vc under hv's pen, REVERSING a ruling vc sent ic on 0452 minutes earlier) ENTRY-LEVEL REGISTER NOTES DO NOT REACH docs/reference, AND THE OMISSION IS DELIBERATE AND SAID IN THE GENERATOR. vc ruled first that they should render, on the premise that 0444's note describes behaviour a user meets; ic read all the entry notes before building and the premise held for one sentence in one note: the field is maintainer rationale in the register's voice, naming nodes, rulings, criterion ids, source paths and its own correction history, and two notes carry security-shaped admissions that are true in the register and not product documentation. Rendering the field would have published all of that. 0452 closes on a line in gen_reference.sh stating that entry notes are the register's rationale and are not rendered (XS, ic's), with a regenerated set unchanged. A reader-facing field is a different design nobody asked for; where a behaviour sentence belongs on a page it goes into that page's prose, and ic's four candidates are recorded in 0452's close as candidates, not work. THE LESSON, again: the ruling was made on one example and the population was read afterwards, by the lane, not by the pen; a ruling about a field is a ruling about every value in it.
